content.comment_body: Can someone assist with a corrupted project file? I'm trying to understand why the system saved it as a modus project rather than the usual .LSC format; this time it saved as .MNP. I might be recycling a project initially made for a [product_name] FS03 unit using [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no]. The original was a Standalone [product_name] [version_no] FS03 from mid-2016. The current setup is a [product_name] [version_no] FS04 with several units sharing network inputs and outputs. I wrote and simulated the program, loaded it onto the main and a feeder unit – all worked fine. After making offline changes, when opening the project and clicking any unit, it enters a repeated 'loading' dialog and I have to force close the task. Is anyone willing to review the file? I prefer not to post the file publicly. Thanks.
If you prefer not to upload the file to the forum, you can send it to me via private message.

Hi, This doesn't seem related to the project itself. I managed to rebuild and load the project into the modules. The original program was corrupted—some module values didn’t apply properly and certain set values kept counting up when they should have stayed static. I reverted to a functional basic version and tried again after a couple of days. Now the project will not fully open on the same PC I used, showing only the list to the left. Selecting a diagram causes the 'loading' dialog to cycle endlessly. The project is stored on my OneDrive and refuses to open on my laptop as well. Could this be caused by too many connections between modules or a mistake in configuration? Or perhaps closing LSC caused issues with Java?
I downloaded your project and was able to open it with the latest version [version_no] without any issues.

Hmm, [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no]? I assure you this issue is genuine. Could a particular setting or preference be responsible? I am running a 64-bit version with the following Java details: Runtime Name: Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment; VM Name: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM; VM Version: 24.51-b03; No DirectDraw: true; Locale: en; Java Home and Working Directory: [url]; Classpath: [url]; Program Version: [version_no]; Timestamp: 2016-07-14 16-34; OS: Windows 8 amd64; Java Memory stats included.

Confirmed, [version_no] resolved the problem. A manual update was necessary. Even though I checked for updates in the application, it always said 'no update available,' and the official download page only lists '[version_no] (SP1)'. I lost several days to this, but at least it's working now and hopefully uploading the project to equipment will succeed. Thanks [user_name].
The service pack 1 (SP1) for [version_no] updates it to [version_no] after installation: [version_no] --> install SP1 --> [version_no].

The naming is confusing: you call it [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no]. The software reports [version_no], the website shows [version_no] (SP1), and the application says there’s no update. The forum release notes, which I just saw, mention [version_no] (SP1). So, is there now a "[version_no].1"? Just a versioning joke. The important thing is it's resolved.

No, there will be no service pack for [version_no]. The next service pack will be SP2 for [version_no]. The final digit refers to the service pack number: [version_no] ---> install SP2 ---> [version_no].2

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced problems opening and using project files owing to inconsistencies between file formats and installed [product_name] Soft Comfort versions. The update system did not alert users to the availability of a recent patch ([version_no]), resulting in extended troubleshooting and work delays. Conflicting version names across the software interface, the website, and installers added to user confusion about which version was needed or actually installed.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable backward compatibility for project files, an effective update notification system, and clear, consistent information on both software and official web pages about which versions and service packs are available.
